title: Nonderogatory matrix characterization: μ_M = χ_M iff cyclic vector

problemStatement.formal: \text{For } M \in M_n(K), \; \mu_M = \chi_M \iff \exists v \in K^n \text{ s.t. } \{v, Mv, \ldots, M^{n-1}v\} \text{ is a basis}
problemStatement.plain: A matrix M over a field K is nonderogatory (its minimal polynomial equals its characteristic polynomial) if and only if it has a cyclic vector v such that {v, Mv, M²v, ..., M^{n-1}v} forms a basis of K^n.
whyMatters: Connects spectral theory to cyclic module structure

proven: Forward direction: cyclic vector → minpoly = charpoly (0 sorries)
Bridge lemma: monic polynomials with divisibility and same degree are equal
Degree characterization: nonderogatory iff deg(minpoly) = n
Full equivalence (using axiom for backward direction)
open: Backward direction: nonderogatory → cyclic vector (axiomatized, needs PID structure theorem)

currentState.nextAction: Backward direction could be proved using PID module theory from Mathlib

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: Forward direction of nonderogatory characterization proved (0 sorries). Backward direction axiomatized. Full equivalence stated.
builtItems: IsCyclicVectorLI definition (linear independence formulation) in CayleyHamiltonMinpolyOQ04.lean
insights: The annihilator formulation of cyclic vector (no nonzero polynomial of degree < n annihilates v) gives a much cleaner forward direction proof than the linear independence formulation
The forward direction proof is beautifully simple: minpoly annihilates M, so it annihilates v, giving a nonzero polynomial in the annihilator if deg < n
Bridge lemma (monic divisor with same degree = equal) is a clean self-contained result useful beyond this problem
Backward direction requires substantial module theory infrastructure (PID structure theorem or JNF)
mathlibGaps: Structure theorem for f.g. modules over PID (partial in Mathlib but not in ready-to-use form for this application)
Rational canonical form not in Mathlib
nextSteps: The backward direction could potentially be proved by deploying Mathlib's PID module theory
Over algebraically closed fields, could use existing JNF axioms from OQ01 to prove backward direction
